# `ctx.publishState` — state-shaped tools

A **state-shaped tool** publishes its current snapshot rather than streaming events. Clients reconnecting mid-run receive the latest snapshot — never event history.

```ts
defineTool({
  name: 'search:semantic',
  state: z.object({
    results: z.array(z.object({ id: z.string(), score: z.number() })),
    progress: z.number(),
    phase: z.enum(['embedding', 'querying', 'ranking', 'done']),
  }),
  handler: async (args, ctx) => {
    ctx.publishState({ results: [], progress: 0, phase: 'embedding' });
    const embedded = await embed(args.query);
    ctx.publishState({ results: [], progress: 0.4, phase: 'querying' });
    const results = await query(embedded);
    ctx.publishState({ results, progress: 1, phase: 'done' });
    return results;
  },
});
```

## Why state-shaped instead of events?

Most streaming tools today emit events (`ctx.emit('progress', …)`, `ctx.emit('text-delta', …)`) and rely on a replay ring buffer (T2.2) to recover from disconnects. That's the right shape when output is **append-only** (LLM token streams). But for tools whose output is a **current value that supersedes prior values**, replay is the wrong shape:

| Aspect | Event-shaped (`ctx.emit`) | State-shaped (`ctx.publishState`) |
|---|---|---|
| Wire form | typed events on the wire | one `snapshot` SSE event per change (see [Client-side consumption](#client-side-consumption)) |
| Replay on reconnect | Last N events from ring buffer | Latest snapshot |
| Memory | Linear in stream length | Bounded by state shape |
| Long-lived disconnect | Buffer evicts past the tool's `replayBufferSize` | Snapshot persists across disconnects |
| Workspace switch | Buffers cleared | Snapshots cleared |

For a search tool with 100 results, state-shape is ~10KB regardless of how many internal updates happened. For a token stream, that same encoding would be lossy.

The ring buffer has no universal eviction threshold: the dispatcher's effective cap is the per-tool `replayBufferSize` and defaults to `0` (no buffer at all) when unset — `const replayCap = tool.state ? 0 : (tool.replayBufferSize ?? 0)`. Several long-stream tools opt into `replayBufferSize: 5000` (`plans:resume`, `plans:launch`, `architect:chat`, `oracle:chat`, `agent_chats:chat`); a tool that sets a different size evicts at that size. State-shaped tools force the cap to `0` and never buffer.

The on-the-wire event name differs by transport adapter. The chat-surface route this page directs you to — `GET /api/operator/state-snapshot`, consumed by `useStateSnapshots()` — emits the SSE event named `snapshot`. The voice converse route (`/api/agent-mcp/operator-converse`) is the only adapter that emits an event named `state-snapshot`.

## Declaring a state-shaped tool

Add `state: StandardSchemaV1` to `defineTool` — any [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev) validator (Zod, Valibot, ArkType, …), not just Zod, since the core stopped being Zod-locked (P-020). The schema is the source of truth for the snapshot shape:

```ts
defineTool({
  name: 'whatever',
  state: z.object({ /* your shape */ }),
  ...
})
```

Tools that declare `state` automatically:
- Get `ctx.publishState` installed (when the call has both `workspaceId` and `runId` — the HTTP catch-all defaults a `runId` per-request, so plain JSON / SSE callers both work).
- Opt **out** of the replay ring buffer (no double-storage — state snapshots replace events on the wire).
- Become **streamable** — the HTTP catch-all's strict-streamable predicate recognizes `tool.state` as a valid trigger for `Accept: text/event-stream`, so the runId-bearing SSE path is reachable even when no `events` are declared.
- Persist snapshots for 5 minutes after run-end (reconnect window).

## Handler API

```ts
ctx.publishState(snapshot)
```

- **Validated** against `tool.state` at publish time via the schema's `~standard.validate` (Standard Schema, P-020) — synchronously, since `publishState` is fire-and-forget and can't await an async validator. Bad shapes throw synchronously.
- **Replaces** the run's current snapshot (v1 is snapshot-only).
- **Reactive** — every call bumps the run's `version` and re-emits to subscribed clients.

### Graceful degradation when there's no state channel

`ctx.publishState` is only installed when the call has **both** a `workspaceId` and a `runId`. Handlers MUST guard for its absence rather than assume it exists — the framework-blessed degradation is an `isError` result carrying the code `no_state_channel`:

```ts
async handler(args, ctx) {
  if (!ctx.publishState) {
    return {
      content: [{ type: 'text', text: JSON.stringify({
        error: 'no_state_channel: <tool> requires a runId-bearing context',
      }) }],
      isError: true,
    };
  }
  // …publish snapshots normally
}
```

The canonical example tool `dev:state_counter` (`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/dev/state_counter.ts`) does exactly this. The HTTP projection surfaces the same `no_state_channel` contract when the JSON path can't supply a `runId`.

### v1 limitations

- **Snapshot-only.** Passing a JSON-Patch array throws. Deltas are deferred to v1.1 once we measure full-snapshot perf on real tools.
- **In-process state.** Snapshots live in the operator's Node process. The registry is stashed on `globalThis` via a `Symbol.for('papercusp.stateChannelRegistry')` key — the same pattern the replay buffer uses — so dev HMR / module re-imports do **not** lose state. A full Node process (server) restart does drop them. PG-backed persistence is a follow-up.

## Client-side consumption

The workspace-scoped SSE stream (`GET /api/operator/state-snapshot`, emitting `snapshot` events) carries `toolState` alongside `openCards`. Use `useStateSnapshots()` to subscribe and `selectToolStates()` to filter:

```ts
import { useStateSnapshots, selectToolStates } from '@/lib/use-state-snapshots';

function MyComponent() {
  const { cards, connected, byRun } = useStateSnapshots();
  const states = selectToolStates(byRun);
  // cards: flattened OpenCardWithRun[] across all open runs (primary product for card rendering)
  // connected: EventSource open state
  // byRun: Map<runId, SnapshotEnvelope>
  // states is Map<runId, toolState>
}
```

The `useStateSnapshots` hook owns one EventSource per mount. `selectToolStates` is a pure helper — do not call `useStateSnapshots()` from inside it.

### Reconnect comes from the workspace route, not per-tool replay

A state-shaped tool's reconnect resilience is delivered by this workspace-scoped `/api/operator/state-snapshot` SSE, **not** by the per-tool streaming SSE's `Last-Event-ID` replay path. On connect, the route replays `snapshotWorkspace()` — a snapshot of every currently-open run in the workspace — then live-fans-out subsequent changes via `subscribeWorkspace`. The per-tool streaming SSE only replays when `replayBufferSize > 0`, and state tools force their cap to `0`, so it never replays them.

## How state-shape absorbs T4.3

The original Phase-4 plan had T4.3 "long-lived disconnected tools" as a separate Tier-4 item: detach `AbortSignal` from disconnect, manage the ring buffer's lifetime, decide when to *actually* abort.

State-shape collapses T4.3 to **zero engineering**:
- State outlives any single SSE connection.
- Reconnect serves the current snapshot — no buffer to evict, no history to replay.
- "Long-lived" is the default for state-shaped tools.

The tool author opts in by declaring `state`. The framework handles the rest.

## When NOT to use state

- **LLM token streams** (`runAgentChat` etc.) — those are inherently append-only. Use `ctx.emit('text-delta', …)` with `replayBufferSize` for reconnect.
- **One-shot tools** with a final result — no streaming, no need for state.
- **Tools that need to emit ordered events** (notifications, log lines) — state collapses ordering into "latest only."

For a tool that mixes a state-shaped result (`results`) with an append-only side stream (`log_lines`), declare `state` AND `events` — both surfaces work together.

## Reference implementation

`dev:state_counter` (`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/dev/state_counter.ts`) is the in-repo proof-of-concept and E2E verification fixture for `ctx.publishState`. It declares a `state` schema, ticks a counter, and calls `ctx.publishState` once per tick with abort handling (`if (ctx.signal.aborted) break;`) and the `no_state_channel` guard above. It backs the `/dev` demo.
